proof: THE PRINTED COLUMN HEADER, VERBATIM AND IN ORDER, READ OFF THIS PAGE (rule 13b.4): `PROGRAM NAME` | `APPROPRIATED FORWARD` | `TOTAL FUNDS AVAILABLE` | `TOTAL EXPENDED` | `TOTAL ENCUMBERED` | `BALANCE TO REVENUE`, under the heading `TOWN OF LUNENBURG / GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS / SUMMARY & CLASSIFICATION OF ACCOUNTS / FISCAL YEAR 2011`. WHY THAT HEADER MATTERS HERE. CLAUDE.md rule 13 names FY2011 as this archive's worked example of a check with no power to fail: `v1` in the generic annual-report extracts means THE FIRST COLUMN OF THIS PAGE THAT HELD FIGURES, the ruler is built per page, and summing v1 across a run adds one page's APPROPRIATED to another's TOTAL EXPENDED -- FY2011 came out within 1% of its own printed total that way. On every appropriations page of this report the first money column is `APPROPRIATED FORWARD`: an appropriation, or a prior-year carry-forward where the cell is followed by the word `fwd`, or a short-term borrowing where it is followed by `srt`. HOW THE TABLE IS SHAPED. Each department prints its line items (Payroll, Other Expenses, and where it applies a bare carry-forward or short-term borrowing on the heading row) and then an UNLABELLED rule-and-total row carrying up to all five columns. The line items are recorded here as `line` rows, so they are published and NOT summed and NOT identity-checked; the department total rows are the `fund` rows and carry the check. ROWS ARE KEYED BY PRINTED POSITION: `Payroll` and `Other Expenses` are printed under almost every department, so `fund_number` is the department's ordinal down the page and, for a line item, that ordinal plus the item's ordinal within the department. Nothing on this page is keyed on a printed name. A department whose total row prints no `BALANCE TO REVENUE` cell is left with NO VALUE in that column rather than a zero, so nothing asserts an identity the page does not state (the FY2014 case where absent was scored as zero and read as the town's arithmetic failing). WHY THIS PAGE WAS READ AT ALL. It was already marked `proven` in the page tracker and had NO page-read behind it, while every one of its rows in the generic extract `report-appropriations.csv` carries `status = check failed`. A page proven by nothing that can fail is the shape rule 13 warns about, and FY2011's appropriations run is the archive's own named case of it. Pages 61 and 62 of this run were read earlier; 60, 63, 64 and 65 were not. WHAT PROVES IT. The page prints no grand total, so the proof is the identity the table states about itself on every department total row -- total funds available less total expended less total encumbered is the balance returned to revenue -- DECLARED here and re-asserted by `verify_page_reads.py` on every run. BEYOND THAT, and recomputed by the generator before it would write anything, every department's LINE ITEMS foot to its own total row in each of the four money columns the department prints: 13 column-ties across 14 departments on this page, all closing to the cent. The generator REFUSES to write if any one of them misses. THE PAGE'S OWN ODDITIES, TRANSCRIBED AS PRINTED. Printed folio 62; the page runs under `UNCLASSIFIED` and then the printed headings `DEBT AND INTEREST`, `STATE & COUNTY ASSESSMENTS` and `TRANSFERS TO OTHER FUNDS`. TWO BLOCKS CARRY A TOTAL ROW AND THE REST ARE SINGLE ROWS: `Total Insurance` is the only LABELLED total row anywhere in this six-page run, and the State & County Assessments block closes on an unlabelled rule-and-total row. The seven assessment sub-rows each print their OWN balance, so they are `line` rows and are neither summed nor identity-checked, exactly as the department line items are. THREE BALANCES ARE PRINTED IN PARENTHESES and are transcribed as negative, which is the only sign that makes the page's own arithmetic close: Court Judgments `($90,000.00)` -- $90,000 spent against nothing appropriated -- Motor Vehicle Excise Surcharge `($600.00)`, Choice Tuitions `($70,536.00)` and the assessments total `($5,210.00)`. `Court Judgments` prints $0.00 in BOTH the appropriated and the available columns, which is a printed zero and not an absent cell. Two rows print a bare figure on the heading line followed by `fwd`. THE PAGE ALSO PRINTS A LEGEND BENEATH THE GRAND TOTAL: `fwd - forward from FY 2010 $248,787.42` and `srt - Salary Reserve Transfer $8,600.00`. BOTH ARE TRANSCRIBED NOWHERE AND NEITHER RECONCILES TO THIS READING: the cells actually annotated `fwd` across pages 60 to 65 come to about $42,584 and those annotated `srt` to about $3,283. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH is what the legend counts -- carry-forwards elsewhere in the report, carry-forwards folded into line items without an annotation, and a figure for a different population all fit equally, and nothing on these six pages distinguishes them. It is recorded here as an open question rather than reconciled.
